title: Aviation Ordnance Weapons and Tactics Instructor (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (6502), DC AVN
raw_text:
2. MOS 6577, Aviation Ordnance Weapons and Tactics Instructor (II/III)
(LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (6502), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Ordnance Officer, qualification/certification board
chairperson or staff billet are subject matter experts (SME) on the tactical
employment of expeditionary aviation ordnance operations. AO WTI Marine
Officers support MAGTF and squadron commanders by maintaining safety and
operational standards, readiness levels and possess the knowledge required to
successfully plan, brief, and execute any technique, tactic or procedure
authorized in our warfighting doctrine. They are intimately familiar with
all aspects of leading an ordnance division/department in any expeditionary
environment or operation. They are experts in forward arming refueling
points/forward operational bases/ distributed aircraft operations and
expeditionary advanced based operation concepts.

       b.   Prerequisites.   Must hold a 6502 MOS.

    c. Requirements. Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 Expeditionary
Ordnance Course (MEOC) (M14G221).


                                         1-248                       Enclosure (1)
 1137                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



    d. Duties. As an Expeditionary Ordnance Subject Matter Expert, they
must be able to effectively and accurately articulate current and future
capabilities of a unit’s ordnance division/department based on current
structure, manpower and qualifications. Identify potential problems and
solve all issues related to logistical considerations, requirements and
capabilities, execution, potential contingencies and retrograde of all
weapons and personnel while observing and adhering to all orders and
regulations regarding explosive safety. Increase the squadron commander’s
capability and lethality by creating, providing and briefing innovative
solutions and improvements to plans, minimizing risk and increasing combat
effectiveness. Responsible for providing the most capable and highest
trained ordnance division/department to commanders IOT accomplish any given
task.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.




                                         1-249                   Enclosure (1)
 1138                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
